experiments.description: Benchmark of standard gate-model QAOA on random k-body spin graphs with nearest-neighbor square-lattice connectivity, measuring CNOT resources as a function of interaction count, interaction order, and system size.

hyperparameters.phase_gadget_cost_model: 2(n-1) CNOTs per n-body interaction before routing

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Random logical spin Hamiltonians containing only σz terms up to k-body interactions; each interaction term is implemented directly as a phase gadget in the gate model.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Implement one QAOA phase-separation cycle for a k-body Ising-like Hamiltonian on a square lattice.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H = sum_i J_i σ_z^(i) + sum_{i<j} J_ij σ_z^(i)σ_z^(j) + sum_{i<j<k} J_ijk σ_z^(i)σ_z^(j)σ_z^(k) + ...

problem_instance.description: Randomly generated k-body graphs with only k-body couplings for fixed k, plus mixed k-body graphs for varying interaction orders.

dataset_specification.description: 10 random instances per setting; for mixed graphs, N in {9,10,11,12} and interaction multiplicities nk chosen from specified discrete sets; for fixed-k graphs, N varied and K in the stated ranges.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Random logical graphs constructed and transpiled to a square lattice using t|ket⟩.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Average CNOT counts over 10 random instances per setting; standard deviation of the mean reported.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Random instance generation; circuit construction for each graph.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Linear fits of CNOT count versus interaction count; averaging over instances.

results.unit: CNOT gates per added interaction term

speedup_claims.factor: lower CNOT count than standard gate-model QAOA for higher-order and larger instances
speedup_claims.baseline_method: standard gate-model QAOA on nearest-neighbor square lattice
speedup_claims.conditions: for k-body graphs with higher interaction order and/or larger logical system sizes
speedup_claims.caveats: No single universal crossover point is given; results are based on averaged transpiled circuits and CNOT counts, not runtime or solution quality.

experiments.description: Benchmark of parity-compiled QAOA using CNOT gates for the same random k-body spin-graph family, comparing parity constraints against direct gate-model embedding on a square lattice.

hyperparameters.constraint_count_relation: NC = K - N (assuming no ancilla qubits and no symmetries)

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Parity mapping of a general σz-only Hamiltonian into physical qubits representing interaction terms plus parity constraints.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Implement one QAOA cycle for the parity-encoded Hamiltonian with local constraints.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Parity constraints enforced as 3- or 4-body interactions; no ancilla qubits assumed.

problem_instance.description: Random k-body graphs and mixed-order graphs used to compare parity-compiled versus standard gate-model resource counts.

dataset_specification.description: For fixed-k benchmarks, 10 random instances per N; for mixed-order benchmarks, 10 random logical graphs per parameter combination.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Parity compilation assumed no ancilla qubits and no logical symmetries.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Average CNOT counts and gate ratios computed from transpiled circuits.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Parity compilation of logical Hamiltonians into local constraints.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: CNOT-count comparison against standard gate model; gate-ratio calculation.

speedup_claims.factor: fewer CNOT gates than standard gate-model QAOA for higher-order and larger instances
speedup_claims.conditions: nearest-neighbor square lattice; no ancilla qubits; no logical symmetries; parity constraints implemented with CNOTs
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states the parity scheme is advantageous for larger systems and higher-order terms, but does not provide a single universal numeric speedup factor for all cases.

speedup_claims.factor: at least about 2x fewer multi-qubit gates in the parity scheme under a simplified lower-bound argument
speedup_claims.conditions: assuming each nontrivial interaction needs at least 2 CNOTs and ignoring SWAP optimization effects
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a rough lower-bound argument, not an empirical benchmark; SWAP gates are not included in the estimate.

experiments.description: Benchmark of parity-compiled QAOA using native 4-body couplers for the same random k-body spin-graph family, comparing multi-qubit gate counts against standard gate-model CNOT implementations.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Parity-compiled Hamiltonian with each constraint realized as a single 4-qubit gate.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Implement one QAOA cycle with plaquette-compiled parity constraints.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Same parity Hamiltonian as in exp_2, with 4-body coupler realization of constraints.

problem_instance.description: Same synthetic random k-body graph benchmarks as the parity-CNOT and standard gate-model comparisons.

dataset_specification.description: Random logical graphs; same benchmark families as in the paper's k-body and mixed-order studies.

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Comparison of total multi-qubit gate counts and gate ratios.

implementation_details.transpilation_target: plaquette chip / square lattice with nearest-neighbor connectivity
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Parity compilation with native 4-body gate assumption.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Gate-count ratio analysis versus standard CNOT-based implementation.

speedup_claims.factor: always fewer multi-qubit gates than standard CNOT-based implementation
speedup_claims.conditions: native 4-body couplers available; parity-compiled plaquette chip
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states the parity scheme with 4-body couplers is always below the standard model even without SWAPs; exact numeric ratios are not provided in text.

speedup_claims.factor: up to 6x reduction in multi-qubit gate count relative to assuming 6 CNOTs per parity constraint
speedup_claims.conditions: when replacing each 4-body parity constraint by a single native 4-body coupler
speedup_claims.caveats: This is an architectural equivalence argument, not a measured benchmark.

experiments.description: Benchmark of the financial crash prediction model encoded as a high-order polynomial Hamiltonian, comparing parity-compiled QAOA resource counts against direct gate-model implementation for synthetic financial networks.

algorithm.variant: parity-compiled QAOA for financial crash model

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Institution market values are discretized into q=5 binary bits per institution; Heaviside step functions are approximated by a truncated Fourier-Legendre expansion, yielding a polynomial σz Hamiltonian.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize F(v) = [v - \tilde{C}(1-C)^{-1}(Dp - b(v,p))]^2, where equilibrium corresponds to the global minimum.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: No explicit constraints beyond the polynomial encoding of the crash condition; truncation/chopping used to reduce Hamiltonian terms.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H_p = Poly_{2r}(σ_z^(i,k)) with r=3, i.e. a polynomial of degree 6 in Pauli-z operators.

problem_instance.description: Synthetic financial networks with 3 or 4 institutions and 7 assets; random ownership and holding matrices.

dataset_specification.description: Randomly generated ownership and holding matrices; minimum self-holding ratio 0.5; asset prices sampled in [5,20]; beta_i = 15% of equity values; critical values vc_i = 80% of original market values.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Binary discretization of market values with q=5 bits; Fourier-Legendre expansion of the Heaviside function truncated at r=3; optional term truncation by n_terms_trunc or coefficient threshold c_thres.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 10 random instances per configuration; resource counts compared across truncation settings and between parity and standard gate-model embeddings.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Construction of financial-network Hamiltonian from ownership/holding matrices and polynomial approximation of the crash condition.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Comparison of CNOT counts and gate ratios for parity vs standard embedding; analysis versus n_terms_trunc and c_thres.

speedup_claims.factor: parity embedding outperforms standard gate-model embedding in CNOT count, especially when many Hamiltonian terms are retained
speedup_claims.conditions: synthetic financial networks; 3 or 4 institutions; q=5 bits per institution; r=3; varying truncation by n_terms_trunc or c_thres
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper does not provide exact numeric CNOT counts in text; the comparison is shown in figures.

speedup_claims.factor: parity with native 4-body couplers is better than parity with CNOT constraints for all truncation settings
speedup_claims.baseline_method: parity constraints implemented with CNOT gates
speedup_claims.conditions: same financial crash benchmark; native 4-body couplers available
speedup_claims.caveats: Exact numeric ratios are not stated in text.

experiments.description: Benchmark of the electronic-structure-to-σz mapping for H2 and LiH, comparing parity-compiled QAOA resource counts against direct gate-model implementation for different Hilbert-space replication factors.

algorithm.variant: parity-compiled QAOA for electronic structure Hamiltonians

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Electronic-structure Hamiltonians are mapped to a σz-only Hamiltonian by replicating the Hilbert space r times; fermionic operators are first mapped to qubit operators using a binary code transform.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Find the ground-state energy of the molecular Hamiltonian via the minimum eigenvalue of the mapped σz Hamiltonian.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Parity constraints in the parity-compiled version; no explicit constraints in the direct gate-model version beyond the mapped Hamiltonian.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H' = sum_i f_i σ_z^(i) + sum_{i,j} f_ij σ_z^(i)σ_z^(j) + sum_{i,j,k} f_ijk σ_z^(i)σ_z^(j)σ_z^(k) + ...

problem_instance.description: Molecular electronic-structure benchmarks for H2 and LiH after active-orbital reduction and binary-code qubit mapping.

dataset_specification.description: H2 with both molecular orbitals active; LiH with three active orbitals (instead of all six) due to resource limits; qubit operators obtained via openfermion binary code transform.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Second-quantized electronic Hamiltonian mapped to qubit operators; then transformed to σz-only form via Hilbert-space replication.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Resource comparison across replication factors r; threshold where parity uses fewer CNOTs reported for H2 and LiH.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Binary-code transform of fermionic Hamiltonians using openfermion; Hilbert-space replication to obtain σz-only Hamiltonian.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Comparison of CNOT counts and gate ratios for parity vs standard embedding; analysis versus replication factor r.

speedup_claims.factor: parity mapping uses fewer CNOT gates beyond a replication-factor threshold
speedup_claims.baseline_method: direct gate-model implementation of the mapped sigma_z Hamiltonian
speedup_claims.conditions: H2 threshold at r = 5; LiH threshold at r = 2; no ancilla qubits; no post-optimization of parity circuit
speedup_claims.caveats: Exact CNOT counts are not given in text; thresholds are inferred from the figure description.

speedup_claims.factor: native 4-body couplers further reduce gate counts below the CNOT-based parity implementation
speedup_claims.baseline_method: parity constraints implemented with CNOT gates
speedup_claims.caveats: No exact numeric ratios are stated in text.
